items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: In fact, Paul Gayten's uncle, whose name was Brother Reed, had a place over there across the river

ctx.x: through, Earl 'Fatha' Hines... And then they would have parties for different bands; after they finished in Jackson, they'd go across the river. Because things ran all night across the river. Everything went across the river, you know.

In fact, Paul Gayten's uncle, whose name was Brother Reed, had a place over there across the river, where they used to play Cotch (that's a three-card gambling game), and Skin, Georgia Skin, all those cold-blooded games, you know, where you bet every turn of the card. And I used to work in there with Paul... They would have four or five fights a night, you know, turn out the place. And Paul used to make me sit up on top of the piano, so if they had a fight I'd just jump over behind the piano, see. [LAUGHS…
Oh, but it was over there on an all dirt road, no pavement over there, you know. And it would rain, and it would be muddy. And we just...
